record.what_it_does: Intapp DealCloud: CRM and deal management platform for financial services firms.
record.auth_notes: The REST API uses the OAuth2 client credentials flow: POST {baseUrl}/api/rest/v1/oauth/token with client_id, client_secret and scope. The secret is a per-user API key. A user generates it on their own Profile page (API Key > Enable), and only after an admin has turned on the 'API' capability for their user group. Scopes are user_management, data, publish, ri_import and backup. Tokens expire after 900 seconds and have no refresh token, so you repeat the flow. There is no third-party authorization-code OAuth for the REST API. The MCP server (https://[tenant].my.intapp.com/mcp/celeste/DealCloud) uses per-user OAuth with discovery and needs no client ID or secret, but it only supports listed AI clients. A multi-user toolkit would have to collect each customer's tenant URL plus a client ID and API key.
record.access_notes: You need a licensed DealCloud tenant, which is enterprise-only with no public pricing (Vendr reports a median buyer spend of about $146k). Within a tenant, an admin must enable the 'API' capability for a user group before a user can create an API key. Intapp's sandbox policy excludes DealCloud – Financial Services from the default free sandbox. A UAT instance costs extra. MCP access needs a 'DealCloud with Celeste' license and the 'MCP Access' capability.
record.api_breadth_notes: The documented areas are Schema, Data (rows, cells, files, history, merge, delete, reports), User Management, Publications (a polled event stream), Site Backups, Relationship Intelligence import, and Schema Contracts. SDKs exist for Python, the Intapp REST Client and C#. The schema is dynamic and varies by tenant. The MCP side also has 'Available Tools' and 'Custom MCP Servers' pages.
record.mcp_notes: Intapp hosts the MCP server per tenant at https://[tenant].my.intapp.com/mcp/celeste/DealCloud (copied from Tools > MCP Servers). Auth is per-user OAuth with discovery. It needs a 'DealCloud with Celeste' license and the MCP Access capability, and write tools must be toggled on by an admin. Supported clients are Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot Studio and Cursor, plus some local clients once enabled. Clients not on that list need to contact their Account Manager.
record.blocker_notes: The docs are public, but every credential lives inside a licensed enterprise tenant. There is no free sandbox for DealCloud FS, and the UAT instance is paid. A toolkit could use per-customer client ID and API key auth against tenant URLs, but building and testing it needs a tenant from Intapp or a customer. Third-party MCP clients that aren't on Intapp's list need Account Manager approval. There are no push webhooks. Events come from polling Publication topics.
